post.text: “Proficient in SQL" = six keywords and knowing what to ask. #sql #programming #techcareer #jobhunting #techtok

scenes.said: Proficient in SQL. Well, I've seen production SQL 200 lines and this is something that I've never understood.
Well, nobody writes all of that lines in one day. Proficient just means like knowing six keywords.
Select, from, where, joined, grouped by, and ordered by. That's most of the job.
Ah, that can't be true. The
The actual work is the questions like how many users signed up last week. Which product sells the most? You translate those questions into keywords. And
over the years, layer by layer. And whoever wrote them googled half of it.
So how do I practice like it's real work?
Well, grab a sample database, write 10 questions business would ask, answer them in SQL, and put it on your GitHub.
That's actually a secret. Being proficient in SQL is like a Tuesday, not a superpower.
This one also says strong CS fundamentals, but I don't have a degree.
